newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Investment funds buy 51 pct in Romania's Policolor.
newsitem.headline: Investment funds buy 51 pct in Romania's Policolor.

text.p: Two foreign investment funds have won a tender to buy 51 percent in Bucharest bourse first-tier dye maker Policolor, the State Ownership Fund (FPS) said on Tuesday.
It said the Romanian-American Enterprise Fund (RAEF) and the Romanian Investment Fund (RIF) had purchased a majority stake in Policolor offered by the FPS, the company's main holder.
"Right now Policolor is 100 percent in private hands," FPS chairman Sorin Dimitriu said after a ceremony marking the deal.
The remaining 49 percent belongs to private investors who participated in the mass sell-off scheme operated by the government from 1995.
RAEF was set up in 1994 by the U.S. Congress, capitalised with a grant from United States Agency for International Development. It has invested $9 million in Romania so far.
The RIF, founded by international fund management company Alliance Capital and Investmentbank Austria, is a closed-ended $65 million fund dedicated exclusively to Romania.
The two funds bought equal stakes in Policolor, RAEF officials said. Details were not disclosed.
Policolor, one of the Bucharest bourse's most active listings, has capital of 41.42 billion lei. Last year it posted a net profit of 15.71 billion lei versus 6.19 billion previously.
Under the agreement, the buyers have to upgrade production equipment, stimulate exports and keep unchanged the number of employees for two years.
The RAEF and the RIF pledged to invest $12 million to upgrade Policolor.
On Monday, Policolor shares closed at 6,500 lei, down 50 lei from Friday's session.
